cim: IDB report on digitalisation and AI
kihagyva: P3: 48 pont, tendencia 20%, jóváhagyás után fordul
cim_eredeti: IDB report on digitalisation and AI
szoveg_eredeti:
IDB, in its flagship publication, reported broad AI adoption could boost Latin America and the Caribbean GDP by 5.1% over a decade.

The Inter‑American Development Bank (IDB) released its flagship publication, the Development in the Americas series, titled ‘From Digitalisation to Artificial Intelligence: Turning Promises into Productivity‘, highlighting the economic potential of artificial intelligence for Latin America and the Caribbean region, which has struggled with weak productivity growth for six decades. The report analysed how digitalisation and AI could raise productivity and improve public‑service delivery in Latin America and the Caribbean, stating broad adoption of AI could boost the region’s gross domestic product (GDP) by 5.1% over a decade and wages by 4.2% over the same period.

It further highlighted the gaps in the digital foundation, with 35% of adults reported using generative AI in 2025-2026, compared with 43% in European OECD countries and 58% in the United States; 26% of adults in the region reported recent online interaction with government, compared with 70% in OECD countries; 27% of adults report having recently made purchases online, compared with 66% in OECD countries and 63% digitally engaged firms using generative AI, 82% rely on off-the-shelf tools or light adaptations rather than solutions integrated into their operations.

During the release, Ilan Goldfajn, IDB Group President, said, ‘Artificial intelligence can become a powerful accelerator of development, but its benefits will not come automatically. Through the Partnership for AI Adoption, the IDB Group is bringing together governments and leading technology companies to help Latin America and the Caribbean harness AI’s potential to raise productivity and translate those gains into better jobs, better public services, and shared prosperity.’

Further, Laura Alfaro Maykall, IDB chief economist and economic counselor, said, ‘This report provides one of the most comprehensive economic assessments of what digitalization and AI could mean for Latin America and the Caribbean, moving the discussion from potential to evidence. In our research, we quantify how AI could affect productivity, growth, and wages across the region and identify the conditions for countries to capture those gains.’

The report also showcased measurable results with the adoption of digitalisation and AI in nations such as Mexico, Costa Rica, and Brazil, where an AI-based app helped reduce users’ depression by 20%, an electronic single-window system increased export values by 46%, and a digital health platform serves 3.4 million users and has delivered 2 million teleconsultations, respectively.

The report highlighted the potential of digital technologies and artificial intelligence to enhance productivity and improve public service delivery across Latin America and the Caribbean. It also suggested that technology adoption, as plug-and-play alone, is not sufficient; distinct stakeholders must also redesign operational processes, strengthen institutional capabilities, retrain their workforce and adopt new management practices to realise its full potential.

Lastly, it underscored the importance of strong institutions, digital skills, accessible data, robust digital infrastructure and an enabling environment for innovation and technology diffusion across the public and private sectors. It also identified labour mobility as an important factor in ensuring that the benefits of technological transformation are widely distributed. In a nutshell, the report positioned AI as a potential driver of productivity, inclusive growth, and long-term development in the region.

Sameer Gahlot is a certified corporate secretary (equivalent to ICSA, UK NARIC, and MACS) and digital policy practitioner working at the intersection of policy, technology, and sustainability. He is currently working with the National Internet Exchange of India, a not-for-profit organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India.
